titles.title: Mass-Manufacturing and Quality Assurance Solutions in SOFC Value Chain in FCH JU Projects qSOFC and INNO-SOFC

descriptions.description: The poster presents mass-manufacturing and quality assurance solutions in the SOFC value chain for FCH JU projects qSOFC and INNO-SOFC. The targets include reducing cell manufacturing cost to 400 €/kW at a production volume of 10 MW/year and increasing production yield in all parts of the stack manufacturing value chain to above 95% by automation and quality assurance. The methods employed include automated machine vision inspection systems, optimization of cell manufacturing for high-speed manufacturing, and development and validation of relevant quality assurance procedures in the interconnect manufacturing process. The results achieved include higher and more homogeneous cell quality, higher yield, and lower scrap rate throughout production.

sections.sectionContent:
Targets
• Reduce cell manufacturing cost to 400 €/kW at production volume of 10 MW/year
• Increase production yield in all parts of stack manufacturing value chain to above 95% by automation and quality assurance
Methods
• Automated machine vision inspection system to detect faults during cell manufacturing
• Optimization of the cell manufacturing for high-speed manufacturing
Results
• Higher and more homogeneous cell quality
• Higher yield and lower scrap rate throughout production

Targets
• Interconnect manufacturing yield of 95%
• Development and validation of relevant quality assurance procedures in the interconnect manufacturing process
Methods
• Failure mode and effect analysis (FMEA) of interconnect manufacturing process
• Automated laser-scanning of interconnect geometries
• Integrated leak tightness measurement system to check interconnect welds/brazes
Results
• Improved quality of interconnects
• Reduced scrap rate

Targets
• Streamline stack manufacturing process and cut cost by increasing yield and lowering OPEX and CAPEX related to manufacturing infrastructure
• Manufacture stacks for 60 kW INNO-SOFC system
Methods
• Testing and analysis of three different manufacturing and conditioning procedures using 30 stacks
• Statistical analysis of data
Results
• Optimized stack assembly and conditioning processes identified
• Potential cost-reductions corresponding to each process identified

Targets
• System electrical efficiency 60%
• System total efficiency 85%
• High emphasis on cost reduction, 4000 € / kW system cost
Methods
• Effective collaboration throughout the value chain enables optimization of the whole system and its components. Key components are specifically designed and optimized for this system.
Results
• System conceptual design ready, exceeds project targets
• System design enables significant reduction in parts count and assembly time
